descriptor.scene: A SHELF OF SMALL WINGED TOWERS is the subject. A plain wooden shelf runs across the frame at chest height carrying nine small winged block-towers in a loose row, each one slightly different in height and wing posture, matte terracotta and cream, clearly the same family as the winged-startup design. CHRISSY stands at frame RIGHT in her cream blazer, close to the lens and cropped at the waist by the frame edge, reaching out to touch the nearest tower with two fingers, her face in soft warm profile, fond. Ordinary wall behind, one taped printout. No trophy case, no glass, no plaques, no lettering anywhere on or under the shelf.
descriptor._caption: By the wall there is a shelf of small winged towers, one for every startup that took off from this room. Nobody dusts a trophy case here. The founders touch them on the way in, the way you touch a doorframe in a house you grew up in.

prompt: Picture-book spread painted in the warm editorial ink-and-wash register of the FIRST reference image. THE FIRST REFERENCE IMAGE IS A STYLE ANCHOR ONLY. Match it for MEDIUM, BRUSHWORK, PALETTE and LIGHT QUALITY ONLY, and take NO subject from it whatsoever: none of its objects, figures, costume, props, furniture, architecture, period or location may appear in the output unless the scene description below asks for them by name. SCENE: A SHELF OF SMALL WINGED TOWERS is the subject. A plain wooden shelf runs across the frame at chest height carrying nine small winged block-towers in a loose row, each one slightly different in height and wing posture, matte terracotta and cream, clearly the same family as the winged-startup design. CHRISSY stands at frame RIGHT in her cream blazer, close to the lens and cropped at the waist by the frame edge, reaching out to touch the nearest tower with two fingers, her face in soft warm profile, fond. Ordinary wall behind, one taped printout. No trophy case, no glass, no plaques, no lettering anywhere on or under the shelf. THE CAMERA MOVES; NOTHING ELSE DOES. Every person keeps the exact seat, side and place the setting's blocking gives them, and if a BLOCKING PLATE is supplied it is the authority on who sits where: obey it at every distance. Whatever the subject is sitting at, leaning on or standing beside is STILL IN THIS PICTURE, in the near foreground if the camera is close. Everyone else present in this place is STILL PRESENT in the picture, behind or beside the subject, soft and out of focus if they are not the subject, and NOBODY leaves and NO seat empties because the camera came closer. FRAMING, CLOSE-UP. IGNORE THE CAMERA DISTANCE IN THE SUPPLIED REFERENCE PLATE, and only the distance: in that plate the camera is far back, and HERE IT HAS WALKED IN CLOSE TO ONE PERSON WITHOUT ANYTHING ELSE CHANGING. ONE face fills the frame from the chest up and the head alone is at least a third of the frame height. If that person is seated at a table, THE NEAR EDGE OF THAT TABLE AND WHAT IS LAID ON IT RUNS ACROSS THE BOTTOM OF THE FRAME in front of them, because that is where they are sitting. What is behind them is what was actually behind them, closer now and thrown soft. chrissy rendered exactly per the supplied reference images: white woman; long wavy blonde hair worn down center parted past the shoulders; warm wide open bright smile; relaxed cream or white blazer over a simple top default; warm editorial register. CHRISSY: a white woman with long wavy blonde hair worn down, center-parted, past the shoulders, a warm wide-open bright smile, in a relaxed cream or white blazer over a simple top. Quick, generous, lit up by having something to share. Warm-editorial ink-and-wash, never photoreal. Master-first: the hero is the canonical calm, centered, face-on winged block-tower on plain terracotta. Every other use (the tilted climbing favicon, the hand-released cover, the soaring close) is derived as its own render with the locked hero passed as the first input image, never re-invented from prose. A render whose block-tower or wings disagree with the hero is a defect: regenerate from the master. the-room exactly as its reference plate: THE ROOM: one long working room in an ordinary building, the kind a small company grows into rather than commissions. Plain desks pushed together in irregular clusters, mismatched chairs, monitors, laptops, a whiteboard with half-erased diagrams, printouts taped to a wall, mugs, a shelf of well-used books, cables. Big plain windows down one side. No open-plan tech-campus gloss, no branding, no slogans on the walls, no neon, no glass conference boxes. The camera is INSIDE the room at standing or seated eye height, never a lobby shot and never an architectural exterior. The clusters of desks give it depth. People are ordinary in scale and are never arranged to face a leader; if anyone is speaking, the group is loose around them rather than seated in rows. The room is LIVED-IN and a little untidy, with evidence of people everywhere whether or not anyone is in frame: a jacket over a chair back, an open notebook, a half-drunk mug, printouts curling where they are taped up, mismatched chairs pushed at angles. It is NEVER sterile, NEVER a showroom, and NEVER lit dramatically; the light is only ever whatever the room actually has at that hour. RENDER EXACTLY ONE MOMENT IN TIME: one single continuous scene at one time of day, filling the whole frame. Do NOT divide the image, do NOT stack a daytime version above a night version, do NOT show the room twice, and do NOT produce a before-and-after or side-by-side comparison of any kind. One long room, human-scaled, low ceiling rather than an atrium. It should feel like somewhere about a hundred people could work, not a headquarters. THE ONLY CHARACTERS IN THIS IMAGE ARE: chrissy. NOBODY ELSE APPEARS. Do not add any other person, figure, creature, robot, animal or bystander, whatever the style description above may suggest. NEGATIVES: neon, 3D/CGI/Pixar, glossy plastic, HUD/arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic. ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS FULL-BLEED PAINTING that fills the entire canvas edge to edge. This is NEVER a grid, NEVER a multi-panel layout, NEVER a comic page, NEVER a contact sheet, NEVER a study or turnaround sheet, NEVER a collage, and NEVER several framed views side by side. Some reference images supplied to you are multi-panel study sheets; use them ONLY for the identity and design of what they depict, and NEVER copy their panelled layout into the output. The output has exactly ONE camera, ONE moment, and NO internal borders, frames, gutters, or dividing lines of any kind. HANDS. Every hand in this image has EXACTLY FOUR FINGERS AND ONE THUMB, five digits and no more and no fewer, and every person has exactly TWO hands and TWO arms. No sixth finger, no extra thumb, no duplicated or spare limb, and no hand emerging from a place no arm reaches. Two hands that come near each other stay SEPARATE and readable as two hands: they never merge into one mass, never share fingers and never fuse at the knuckles. Each hand is joined to a wrist of believable thickness, the wrist to a forearm, and the forearm to the shoulder of the person it belongs to. Hands are sized to their owner: never oversized, never doll-small. A hand resting ON something makes real contact with THAT thing, with the fingers following its actual surface and not floating above it or sinking into it.
qa: winged-startup: The startup is a HAND-STACKED tower of two or three flat cream blocks, slightly imperfect and uneven, never a single block and never a neat machine-precise stack.
winged-startup: Cream wings are attached to the tower and the whole reads as LIFT: rising, climbing, or airborne, never sitting still on a surface.
winged-startup: Plate register only: flat solid terracotta ground, a single-weight wobbly confident black ink outline, flat ivory-cream fills as the only fills.
winged-startup: Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, UI, or cursor marks, ever.
winged-startup: Face-on and flat: no perspective, no isometric, no parallelograms, no side faces or edge thickness, no shading, no gradients, no coloured linework.
